The relevant dataflow is `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl -> openMSP430.dbg_0.dbg_swbrk -> openMSP430.frontend_0.cpu_halt_req -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. Debug halt and low-power controls can hold the frontend in `I_IDLE`/`E_IDLE` or delay the boundary at which a running instruction completes. Holding or toggling `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl` at a completion boundary can repeatedly withdraw the condition that releases the instruction state machine. Legitimate instructions cease retiring and the processor remains halted or repeatedly re-enters an incomplete execution phase.

`openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl` sets the selected completion class, execution state, or transition into the required terminal state; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.clock_module_0.scan_mux_puc_rst.scan_mode`, `openMSP430.clock_module_0.scan_mux_puc_rst.data_out`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_dst_wr`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`, and the remaining path guards. The relevant dataflow is `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl -> openMSP430.clock_module_0.puc_s -> openMSP430.clock_module_0.puc_pnd_set -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_src_wr -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. For a source-writeback instruction, `exec_done` is produced by `exec_src_wr ? (e_state == E_SRC_WR)`. An attacker who forces `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_ctl` away from its terminal value can keep the selected predicate false on successive `mclk` cycles. Decode and fetch remain blocked waiting for completion, creating a persistent loss of instruction retirement.
